links.title: Chapter 16 - SQLite Databases, Automate the Boring Stuff with Python, 3rd Ed
links.why: The course textbook's own chapter, free online: connecting, CRUD, transactions, foreign keys, backups and the two practice programs.

links.title: sqlite3 - DB-API 2.0 interface for SQLite databases
links.why: The module's tutorial and reference: placeholders, executemany, row factories, the context manager and the three ways of controlling transactions.

links.title: PEP 249 - Python Database API Specification v2.0
links.why: The standard interface behind sqlite3: connections, cursors, parameter styles and why auto-commit must start off.

links.title: What's New In Python 3.13
links.why: Where sqlite3 began to warn about unclosed connections and about positional arguments, and the SQLite version Python now needs.

links.title: SQLite Documentation
links.why: The index of the SQLite project's own documentation: SQL syntax, file format, limits and how-to pages.

links.title: STRICT Tables
links.why: Exactly what STRICT requires and allows: the six column types, coercion and the error for a value that does not fit.

links.title: Datatypes In SQLite
links.why: The five storage classes and type affinity: why an INTEGER column can hold text in an ordinary table.

links.title: SQLite Foreign Key Support
links.why: Parent key rules, why foreign keys are off by default, PRAGMA foreign_keys and the ON DELETE actions.

links.title: Quirks, Caveats, and Gotchas In SQLite
links.why: The project's own list of surprises, among them double-quoted strings read as text when no column has that name.

links.title: SQLite Autoincrement
links.why: How a rowid or INTEGER PRIMARY KEY is chosen, and what AUTOINCREMENT changes about reusing numbers.

links.title: Appropriate Uses For SQLite
links.why: When SQLite fits and when a client/server database is better, including the one-writer rule.

links.title: Transaction
links.why: BEGIN, COMMIT and ROLLBACK, and the DEFERRED, IMMEDIATE and EXCLUSIVE kinds of transaction.

links.title: Command Line Shell For SQLite
links.why: The sqlite3 command-line program the chapter installs: dot commands, headers, dumping and importing.

links.title: DB Browser for SQLite
links.why: One of the graphical programs the chapter names, for looking at and editing a SQLite file without code.

_note: Every url was opened with an HTTP download on the date in 'checked' and its page title read; the titles are those the pages served. The Python documentation pages served on that date were headed Python 3.14.8, while the chapter research read the 3.14.4 sources. The textbook page's own title is the one the page served. No video or discussion thread is listed: none was opened and read, so the page offers labelled searches instead and the course owner may add checked ones here.
